o: Horizontally on the ground
Loose in a corner
Near a heat source for warmth
Stacked on top of each other
Vertically and secured to prevent falling

n.0: Horizontal storage can damage valves and cause leaks.
n.3: Stacking is unsafe and risks crushing cylinders.

10.q: What must you do before using lifting equipment on site?
o: Ask a colleague to try it first
Check the equipment has a current inspection certificate
Ensure it is painted in site colours
Lubricate all moving parts
Test it by lifting a heavy object
10.w: Lifting equipment must have a valid inspection certificate to ensure it is safe for use.

n.4: Testing with a heavy load without checks can be dangerous.
n.0: A colleague’s test is not a substitute for inspection.

10.q: What should be done before entering a confined space on a construction site?
o: Ask a colleague if it looks safe
Carry out a risk assessment and test the atmosphere
Check the weather forecast
Ensure the space is brightly painted
Spray water on the floor

n.2: Weather may be relevant but is not the primary requirement.
n.3: Paint colour has no bearing on safety.
n.0: Visual checks alone are insufficient.
n.4: Spraying water does not make a confined space safe.

10.q: When using a mobile tower scaffold, what must be done before moving it?

Check if the wheels are inflated
Lower the platform to half height
Push it with someone inside to save time
Remove all materials and ensure no one is on the platform

To mark the boundary
To prevent noise
To prevent people or plant from falling in
To store excavated materials

Complete a survey to identify hazards such as asbestos
Knock down small sections to see what happens
Remove only loose debris
Work without machinery for safety

n.3: Removing loose debris is not enough to ensure safety.

To keep equipment away from the edge
To make it easier to climb out
To prevent the sides from collapsing and trapping workers
To stop water collecting

Jump to the surface
Stand on stored materials
Use a rope without knots
Use a secured ladder extending above the top

10.q: Which TWO are true about noise on site?

Ear defenders are optional near loud tools
Hearing damage is permanent
Noise is only a problem indoors
Protection is worn where signed
